verdicts.summary: Lean has an equivalent formula. Same object: an additive increment on the second reserved patch, a coefficient-weighted sum of three fixed nonnegative disjointly supported bumps in the normalized radial variable x_* = X / X_* (Lean: p.1 / patchRadius F XR), with coefficients depending smoothly on eta; the index set is Fin 3 (j = 0,1,2) rather than i = 1,2,3. The one real difference is the prefactor: the paper multiplies the bump sum by e_* alone (its unmodified profile on the patch being E = e_* f(eta) x_*^{-1/2-lambda}), while Lean multiplies by shapedPatchAmplitude F eta = patchAmplitude F * (1 + eta^2)⁻¹, i.e. by e_* f(eta). The identification e_* = patchAmplitude F is fixed by E_on_patch, whose right-hand side is exactly e_* f(eta) x^{-1/2-lambda}. The rewriting: the two families of increments coincide under c_i(eta) ↦ c_i(eta) / f(eta); f(eta) = (1+eta^2)⁻¹ is smooth and bounded in [1/2, 1] on the parameter domain Icc (-1) 1, so the reparametrization is a smooth positive rescaling of the free coefficient function and changes neither the span of the increments nor their smoothness in eta.
